material_dependency_test.basis: The II.C.8 target supplies a synthetic project record with explicit completion criteria, evidence entries, approvals, deliverables, and omissions. Closure-readiness classification therefore does not require first performing II.C.6 documentation-integrity review as a separate capability.

dispositions.rationale: Documentation integrity is useful to project closure, but the bounded closure target carries the record and criteria necessary for independent performance. The evidence supports no mandatory hard prerequisite.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.C.8 target determines closure readiness from supplied completion criteria and project records. It does not require the learner to independently execute II.C.7 project-risk analysis before applying those criteria.

dispositions.rationale: Risk status can be part of a closure record, but risk-analysis capability is not materially required for the evidence-bounded closure classification task. A hard edge would overstate the evidence.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.F.1 assessment supplies observable team behaviors, coordination events, conflicts, decisions, and context. Team-stage/dynamics recognition can therefore be performed without first constructing an organizational communication plan under II.E.2.

dispositions.rationale: Communication and team dynamics interact in practice, but the target capability is independently assessable from team-interaction evidence. The relationship does not satisfy the hard-prerequisite standard.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.F.2 assessment supplies named roles, responsibilities, decision rights, handoffs, and selected gaps. Role/responsibility mapping is therefore independently performable without first identifying team-stage dynamics under II.F.1.

dispositions.rationale: Understanding team dynamics may enrich role discussions, but the role-mapping target has all evidence required for its bounded task. No material hard prerequisite is established.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.F.3 assessment supplies a bounded team decision need, available evidence, participation constraints, and candidate tool or decision-concept classes. Tool selection does not require prior execution of the II.F.2 role-mapping capability.

dispositions.rationale: Role clarity can affect decision practice, but the decision-tool target is independently executable from its supplied decision context. A mandatory II.F.2 prerequisite is not supported.
